title: Rabbi Yehudah of Sikhnin
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman cites the old Tanchuma, Ekev. In his view, the original must have read “R–Y of Sikhnin,” referring to R’ Yehoshua of Sikhnin, who is well known in aggadic literature. Hyman argues that the initials later came to be read as Rabbi Yehudah.

notes.text: The unexplained בל״ם is preserved rather than silently treated as בל״ס, “without doubt.” “Well known in aggadic literature” is an idiom, not the title of a book.

The saved whole Torat Emet TanchumaEikev4:1 explicitly has Rabbi Yehudah of Sikhnin in Rabbi Eliezer’s name. This supports the Yehudah occurrence, not Hyman’s claimed Yehoshua reconstruction or a correction history. His cited Old Tanchuma was not newly inspected. Literal בל״ם is not silently changed to בל״ס or expanded without doubt; if that conjectural reading were established it would carry that force. הנחומא is contextually Tanchuma; well known in aggadic literature is an idiom, not a verified work title. Uninspected Yehoshua’s title remains R'.

The supplied transcription reads בל״ם without a clear expansion. The final letter in the printed notice (vol. II, p. 574) appears to be a samekh, giving the abbreviation בל״ס, “without doubt.” The standard Tanchuma, Ekev 4:1, names Rabbi Yehudah of Sikhnin as the transmitter of Rabbi Eliezer’s saying about nine kav of harmful spirits. A comparison with the main Ekev section of the inspected Buber edition leaves Hyman’s exact old-Tanchuma locus unconfirmed. His proposed expansion of the initials remains an interpretation.
